title: Comparing Affordable Lunch Options
transcript:
We've collected prices from twelve places near the university, but I'm not sure how to turn them into a useful comparison. Some sell complete meals, while others list every item separately.
We need a consistent definition of lunch before comparing prices. Otherwise a small sandwich could appear cheaper than a full meal simply because it includes less food. Did we record portion information?
Only roughly. We noted whether a drink was included, but not the size of the main item. Perhaps we should go back with a standard form and photograph the menus, with permission.
Photographs would help us check the details later. We should also record the distance from campus. A cheap meal may be less practical for someone who has only a short break between classes.
Yes. Walking time would be more useful than a straight line on a map. We could measure from the main library, since that is a familiar starting point for students from several departments.
Agreed, but we shouldn't pretend that everyone starts there. In the presentation, we can describe it as a common reference point. What about the special discounts some places offer only in the late afternoon?
Let's record those in a separate column. Our main comparison should use the normal lunchtime price. Otherwise we would recommend a low price that most students couldn't actually obtain during their break.
That makes sense. We also need to consider dietary requirements. At one cafe, the cheapest main meal contained meat, but the vegetarian alternative cost substantially more. One headline price would conceal that difference.
We could include a separate vegetarian option where one is available. I don't think we should attempt to assess nutritional quality ourselves, though. We don't have the detailed ingredient information or the expertise for that.
Exactly. We can report observable features without giving health advice. Perhaps we should interview a few students about what makes a place usable, such as queues, seating, or the ability to bring food back to campus.
That could improve the recommendations, but we should avoid presenting those interviews as representative of the whole university. If we only speak to people outside our own department, their timetables may be very similar.
Then let's recruit at several campus locations and describe the sample clearly. The final result can be a comparison tool showing trade-offs, rather than a single ranking that suggests the same place is best for every student.

questions.prompt: The students plan to photograph the ____.
questions.explanation: 拍摄菜单可供之后核查价格和餐点细节。

questions.prompt: Walking times will be measured from the main ____.
questions.explanation: 以主图书馆为共同参照点测步行时间。

questions.prompt: Special discounts will be recorded in a separate ____.
questions.explanation: 非正常午餐时段的优惠单列，不混入常规价格比较。

questions.prompt: Why will the students avoid evaluating nutritional quality?
options: The meals are all nutritionally identical
They lack suitable information and expertise
The assignment prohibits any mention of food
questions.answer: They lack suitable information and expertise
questions.explanation: 他们缺乏完整配料信息和专业知识。

questions.prompt: What form should the final result take?
options: One ranking suitable for every student
A tool showing different practical trade-offs
A list containing only the cheapest meal
questions.answer: A tool showing different practical trade-offs
questions.explanation: 最终应呈现不同条件的权衡，不宣称一家适合所有人。
